title: Create and Reopen a Learning Org
summary: Use a browser to create a personal Salesforce learning environment and verify that you can return to the same one.
prerequisites: J01 and J02: the Northstar example and the difference between Salesforce products, the platform, and an org.
A browser and access to a personal Trailhead account.
learningObjectives: Distinguish Trailhead from a Salesforce org.
Create and reopen a named learning environment.
Keep sign-in details out of submitted evidence.

sections.heading: Know which account opens which place
body: Trailhead is Salesforce's learning website. It contains explanations and exercises. A Trailhead Playground is a Salesforce org intended for hands-on learning. Signing in to Trailhead opens the learning website; launching a Playground opens Salesforce itself. They are connected experiences, but they are not the same screen or the same set of stored information.

For this lesson you need a browser and a way to sign in to Trailhead. You do not need Visual Studio Code, a terminal, or programming experience. We introduce those tools when they have a purpose. Use a personal learning environment rather than an employer's working org, and use fictional customers. Northstar is an invented company, not an account you need to obtain from someone else.

callouts.text: The first technical skill is knowing where you are working and how to reopen it.

sections.heading: Create an identifiable Playground
body: Open the official Playground creation lesson linked below and sign in to Trailhead. A hands-on challenge is an exercise that checks work in a selected Salesforce org. Near its Launch control, you can choose an existing org or create a Playground. Interface labels can change slightly; identify the create, select, and launch actions by their purpose.

Give the environment a recognizable name such as SAM Beginner. Wait for creation to finish, then select that environment before launching it. Salesforce opens in another browser tab. If nothing opens, inspect the browser's blocked-pop-up notice before trying repeated creation. Accidentally making several similar environments makes it harder to know where your work lives.

A newly created org may contain sample records and applications. Those records are not Northstar's finished project. The Northstar objects are introduced through configuration or the starter project later. Not seeing Vehicle on your first visit is therefore expected. Do not install an unrelated package just to make the interface resemble a later lesson.

callouts.text: A normal Playground is not a promise of every paid product or Agentforce capability. Specialized lessons state their own environment requirements.

steps.title: Sign in to the learning website
steps.instruction: Open Trailhead and use your chosen sign-in method.
steps.expected: You can access your learning profile.

steps.title: Create or select the org
steps.instruction: Find the hands-on org selector, create SAM Beginner if necessary, and wait for readiness.
steps.expected: The selector identifies the environment you intend to use.

steps.title: Launch Salesforce
steps.instruction: Select that org and choose Launch; allow the new tab if the browser blocks it.
steps.expected: A Salesforce page opens without needing development tools.

steps.title: Inspect without changing
steps.instruction: Locate App Launcher, an available application, and Setup if your learning account permits it.
steps.expected: You recognize the areas introduced in J04.

sections.heading: Prove that the environment is yours to revisit
body: Close the Salesforce tab and launch the same Playground again from Trailhead. Check the selected environment name before launching. Two environments may look almost identical, so visual similarity alone is not sufficient evidence. Record the environment's friendly name and the route you used to reopen it in a private learning note.

A Salesforce username and a contact email can be different. Do not guess credentials or publish them in an assignment screenshot. Trailhead provides a separate lesson for obtaining Playground credentials when a later tool requires them. For today's browser route, successfully reopening the selected org is the important result.

Developer Edition is another kind of environment commonly used for learning and development. If you already have one, discuss whether it fits the upcoming exercises rather than assuming every environment is interchangeable. A new beginner can follow the Playground route consistently. If an application is unavailable, note its absence and ask a precise question; changing random settings is not part of this exercise.

callouts.text: Can you close the tab, select the named environment again, and explain why it is separate from an employer's org?

exercise.title: Record a repeatable entry route
exercise.brief: Prepare a short environment note that helps you resume learning tomorrow.
steps: Record its friendly name and your navigation route.
Record the first Salesforce page you see; omit credentials. You will explore its navigation in J04.
acceptance: The note identifies one learning environment consistently.
No passwords, authentication files, or real customer details appear in the evidence.

knowledgeCheck.question: Is VS Code required for this lesson?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. A browser and a learning org are enough.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why can two orgs look alike?
knowledgeCheck.answer: They may use the same interface and sample configuration while containing separate data.

knowledgeCheck.question: Does a Playground include every Salesforce product?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Product availability and special lesson requirements must be checked separately.

recap: Distinguish Trailhead from a Salesforce org.
Create and reopen a named learning environment.
Keep sign-in details out of submitted evidence.

Restrained professional editorial illustration, flat geometric drawn forms with fine navy linework and a subtle paper texture. Warm ivory #F7F4EE, navy #12253C, muted cobalt #3867E8, restrained teal #138A86 and sage. One clear central scene, generous empty margins, at most three main visual groups. Calm adult learning design. Any people are clearly drawn stylized figures, never realistic photos. NO text, letters, numerals, logos, watermarks, Salesforce mascots, decorative clutter or glossy 3D. Exact topic: Your Learning Org. Subject: a small separate training workspace in a protective outline beside a larger company workspace.
